_about: English mode data (SPEC 1b), 2026-10-16. en_pron: Latin syllables, long vowels doubled (aa, ee, oo), [text, is_special]; special = sounds English lacks (q, kh, ḥ, ‘ ع, ’ ء, ṣ ḍ ṭ ẓ, gh). th (ث) and dh (ذ) exist in English, so not special. Final ة read -ah. audio_en_text is read by Alice (ElevenLabs).

kitab.mean_en: book (in Bangla mostly a religious book)
kitab.note_en: Root ك ت ب means writing. মক্তব (maktab) comes from the same root.
kitab.shift_en: In Arabic any book. In Bangla কিতাব usually means a religious or madrasa book.
kitab.audio_en_text: Kitab. In Arabic, kitaab. It means book.

qalam.note_en: The opening ق comes from the very back of the tongue, not a Bangla ক. Arabic itself took the word from Greek kalamos (reed).
qalam.audio_en_text: Kolom. In Arabic, qalam. It means pen.

khabar.note_en: خ is a rough kh scraped from the throat, harsher than Bangla খ. Do not mix it up with قَبْر (grave).
khabar.audio_en_text: Khobor. In Arabic, khabar. It means news.

qabr.note_en: Khobor and kobor differ only in the first letter: خ against ق.
qabr.audio_en_text: Kobor. In Arabic, qabr. It means grave.

hisab.note_en: ح comes from the middle of the throat, a heavy breathy h. The ordinary h is ه.
hisab.audio_en_text: Hishab. In Arabic, hisaab. It means calculation.

dunya.note_en: Long aa at the end: dun-yaa. Literally the nearer life, the opposite of the hereafter.
dunya.ex_en: The life of this world is short.
dunya.audio_en_text: Duniya. In Arabic, dunya. It means this world.

insaf.note_en: ص is a heavy s: tongue low, mouth full. The plain s is س. Root ن ص ف means half: giving both sides an equal share is justice.
insaf.audio_en_text: Inshaf. In Arabic, insaaf. It means justice.

masjid.note_en: Pattern مَفْعِل means a place: the place of سَجْدَة (prostration).
masjid.audio_en_text: Moshjid. In Arabic, masjid. It means place of prostration.

madrasa.note_en: دَرْس (dars) means lesson, so a madrasa is a place of lessons. To Arabs an ordinary school is also a madrasa.
madrasa.shift_en: In Arabic any school. In Bangla only an Islamic school.
madrasa.ex_en: I go to school every day.
madrasa.audio_en_text: Madrasa. In Arabic, madrasah. It means any school.

ilm.note_en: Starts with ع, a squeezed throat sound Bangla does not have. عَالِم (alem) means a learned person. Everyday Bangla also says এলেম.
ilm.audio_en_text: Ilm. In Arabic, ilm. It means knowledge.

sabr.note_en: The heavy ص again. 'Shobur koro' is really Arabic.
sabr.ex_en: Patience is the key to relief.
sabr.audio_en_text: Shobur. In Arabic, sabr. It means patience.

dua.note_en: ع in the middle, hamza ء at the end (a tiny stop in the throat). In Arabic du-‘aa’, not doa.
dua.audio_en_text: Doa. In Arabic, du-aa. It means asking God.

alim.note_en: Whoever has ilm is an alem. Pattern فَاعِل means the one who does. Arabic starts with ع: ‘aa-lim.
alim.ex_en: His father is a great scholar.
alim.audio_en_text: Alem. In Arabic, aalim. It means a learned person.

ulama.note_en: Plural of alem. Hamza ء at the end, a short stop. Bangla often says ওলামা-মাশায়েখ.
ulama.ex_en: The scholars are the heirs of the prophets.
ulama.audio_en_text: Olama. In Arabic, ulamaa. It means scholars.

talim.note_en: Pattern تَفْعِيل means making someone do it: عَلَّمَ is to teach, so talim is teaching.
talim.shift_en: In Arabic, teaching and education. In Bangla mostly hands-on training or practice.
talim.audio_en_text: Talim. In Arabic, ta-leem. It means teaching.

malum.note_en: Pattern مَفْعُول means the thing acted on: something known. The middle ع got lost in Bangla.
malum.shift_en: In Arabic, known or evident. In Bangla 'malum hoya' means to sense or notice.
malum.audio_en_text: Malum. In Arabic, ma-loom. It means known.

hukm.note_en: Heavy ح at the start. One syllable in Arabic: ḥukm. Bangla added the middle u.
hukm.shift_en: In Arabic mainly a ruling, verdict or rule. In Bangla an order (Arabic for order is أَمْر).
hukm.audio_en_text: Hukum. In Arabic, hukm. It means a ruling.

hakim.note_en: Pattern فَاعِل: the one who rules. Careful: Bangla হাকিম is sometimes used for হেকিম (doctor), which is a different word, حَكِيم.
hakim.audio_en_text: Hakim. In Arabic, haakim. It means ruler or judge.

hakeem.note_en: Pattern فَعِيل shows a quality: very wise. Allah's name al-Hakeem is the same word.
hakeem.shift_en: In Arabic, wise. In the subcontinent it became a Unani doctor.
hakeem.ex_en: My grandfather was a wise man.
hakeem.audio_en_text: Hekim. In Arabic, hakeem. It means wise.

hikma.note_en: The Arabic ending ة became t through Persian: hikmah to hekmot.
hikma.shift_en: In Arabic, wisdom. In everyday Bangla 'hekmot kore' means cleverly, with tact.
hikma.ex_en: There is wisdom in his words.
hikma.audio_en_text: Hekmot. In Arabic, hikmah. It means wisdom.

amal.note_en: ع ل م and ع م ل: the same three letters in a different order. Ilm is knowing, amal is doing.
amal.ex_en: Knowledge without deeds is of no use.
amal.audio_en_text: Amol. In Arabic, amal. It means work.

amla.note_en: Plural of عَامِل (one who works). Bangla আমলাতন্ত্র (bureaucracy) comes from here.
amla.shift_en: In Arabic, workers (plural). Through Persian, a government officer in Bangla. Modern Arabic عُمْلَة means currency, a different word.
amla.audio_en_text: Amla. In Arabic, amalah. It means workers.

mamla.note_en: Pattern مُفَاعَلَة means something done between two sides: mutual dealing. Mu-aamalah shrank to mamla.
mamla.shift_en: In Arabic, dealing or transaction. In Bangla a court case (Arabic for that is قَضِيَّة).
mamla.ex_en: We have a business deal between us.
mamla.audio_en_text: Mamla. In Arabic, mu-aamalah. It means dealing.

mamuli.note_en: Same pattern مَفْعُول as malum. The final i was added later.
mamuli.shift_en: In Arabic, what is done or in force. Urdu and Persian 'mamuli' is ordinary; Bangla, trivial.
mamuli.audio_en_text: Mamuli. In Arabic, ma-mool. It means customary.

maktab.note_en: The root of kitab, ك ت ب, in pattern مَفْعَل = place: the place of writing.
maktab.shift_en: In modern Arabic an office or desk. In Bangla the place where children learn Quran.
maktab.ex_en: My father is at the office.
maktab.audio_en_text: Moktob. In Arabic, maktab. It means office, a place of writing.

majlis.note_en: جَلَسَ means to sit. Majlis is a place of sitting. Same pattern مَفْعِل as masjid.
majlis.shift_en: In Arabic also a parliament or council. In Bangla usually a gathering.
majlis.audio_en_text: Mojlish. In Arabic, majlis. It means a place of sitting.

mahalla.note_en: حَلَّ means to unload and stop. A mahalla is where people stopped and settled.
mahalla.audio_en_text: Moholla. In Arabic, mahallah. It means a town quarter.

mahfil.note_en: حَفَلَ means to gather. Mahfil is the place of gathering. The middle h is the heavy ح.
mahfil.ex_en: We went to a big gathering.
mahfil.audio_en_text: Mahfil. In Arabic, mahfil. It means a gathering.

jamaat.note_en: ج م ع means to gather. The final ة became t through Persian: jamaa‘ah to jamat.
jamaat.audio_en_text: Jamat. In Arabic, jamaa-ah. It means a group.

juma.note_en: The day of gathering. In Arabic Friday is simply يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ.
juma.audio_en_text: Juma. In Arabic, jumu-ah. It means Friday, the day of gathering.

jama.mean_en: deposit, to hand in (money, a form)
jama.note_en: Arabic ends with ع: jam‘. Bangla lost the ع.
jama.shift_en: In Arabic, gathering; in grammar, the plural. In Bangla, depositing money or handing in a form.
jama.ex_en: Kutub is the plural of kitab.
jama.audio_en_text: Joma. In Arabic, jam. It means gathering.

jame.mean_en: the main (Friday) mosque, as in 'jame mosjid'
jame.note_en: Pattern فَاعِل: the one that gathers. The mosque that gathers everyone for Juma.
jame.shift_en: In Arabic jaami‘ alone means the main mosque, and as an adjective 'bringing everything together'. In Bangla only in 'jame mosjid'.
jame.ex_en: I prayed in the big Friday mosque.
jame.audio_en_text: Jame. In Arabic, jaami. It means the mosque that gathers everyone.

salam.note_en: س ل م means being safe, peace. Giving salam is wishing someone peace.
salam.audio_en_text: Salam. In Arabic, salaam. It means peace.

islam.note_en: Pattern إِفْعَال, like insaf. Literally, giving oneself over.
islam.audio_en_text: Islam. In Arabic, islaam. It means submitting to God.

muslim.note_en: Whoever accepts Islam is a muslim. Pattern مُفْعِل means the one who does.
muslim.shift_en: The Arabic word is muslim. Musolman was formed in Persian, then came to Bangla.
muslim.audio_en_text: Musolman. In Arabic, muslim. One who submits to God.

salamat.note_en: The final ة became t through Persian: salaamah to salamot. Arabs say goodbye with مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ.
salamat.shift_en: In Arabic any kind of safety. In Bangla almost only in 'shohi-salamote'.
salamat.audio_en_text: Salamot. In Arabic, salaamah. It means safety.
